notes: Shorthand notes from calls: customer is a legal-tech company building federated enterprise search across case files, contracts, and internal KBs. Priorities: sub-100ms tail latency for first-pass retrieval at 200 qps, rerank within 200-300ms end-to-end, predictable cost per query to compare vs pgvector+cpu cross-encoder approach. Wants connector that supports incremental upserts, deletes, and strong consistency for live documents. Quoted: "Costs blow up when we rerank every top-100 candidate — need selective rerank + server-side support." Interested in Redwood Optimize suggestions for batching + cache TTL to reduce token spend. InfoSec flagged data residency — prefer private control plane + KMS integration. Blocking: VPC peering approval (network), legal sign-off on data residency SLA, final econs vs self-hosted pgvector. Use Pinecone/Weaviate only as fallbacks for certain teams; preferred outcome is Redwood Private with a pgvector connector to our Postgres fleet or a dedicated vector-store managed by Redwood.
requirements_summary: Large-scale RAG search: 50M+ vectors initial target, 200 qps sustained, 95th percentile retrieval <100ms, reranked results within 200-300ms E2E. Connector feature set: bulk async upsert (>=50k vectors/min), incremental delta indexing, soft delete + tombstones, region-aware storage, transactional updates to metadata, vector similarity + metadata filters, hooks for hybrid semantic + lexical (Elastic integration). Security: SSO (SAML), KMS for keys, audit logs per request, retention policies and data residency in us-east-1. Cost target: break-even vs in-house pgvector when per-query total (retrieve+rerank) <= $0.02-0.05 on avg.
indexing_scale: target 50M vectors, expected growth to 200M over 12 months; initial POC subset 1.2M vectors
target_latency: first-pass retrieval p95 <100ms at 200 qps; rerank p95 additional 100-200ms (total <=300ms)
reranking_strategy: client-side lightweight bi-encoder for recall + server-side cross-encoder rerank for precision on top-K candidates. Wants Redwood to support prioritized reranks (top-10) and cost caps.
connector_requirements: Support for Pinecone/Weaviate/pgvector/Elastic connectors. Must provide postgres-compatible pgvector plugin or managed vector-store option; bulk async ingestion endpoint with acking, backpressure handling, idempotent upserts, delete semantics, and TLS+mutual auth for agent-to-store traffic.
poc_scope: 2-week POC: index 1.2M vectors, simulate 200 qps retrieval traffic, run reranker at configurable top-K, measure p50/p95 latency and cost per query. Deliverables: perf report, connector checklist, security sign-off checklist, estimated TCO for managed vs dedicated deployments.
commercial_notes: Customer expects enterprise pricing; looking at $150k-$300k ARR commitment if POC meets latency + security requirements. Prefers 12-month committed dedicated capacity with burst options. Wants clear unit economics: cost per 1k queries breakdown (retrieve + rerank + model cost).
objections: Worry about lock-in to managed vector store; preference for pgvector on their Postgres fleet. Concerned about rerank cost escalation and hidden token charges. Wants clear SLOs and fallback policy when dedicated capacity is saturated.
